card.name: Words leading into scholarly engagement with texts
card.fires_on: Words in academic prose about reading or analyzing texts and scholarship, just before a likely word like engage, interaction or engagement. Typical settings are biblical studies, literary criticism and queer theory.

modes.label: Verbs and links before study
modes.description: Words such as require, to or engaging that lead into reading or reviewing literature.
modes.example: essays require arguments which in turn<< require>> the reading of secondary literature.

modes.label: Modifiers before analysis
modes.description: Adjectives or ordinals placed before a noun like analysis or understanding in scholarly writing.
modes.example: Alisha Knight provides the<< first>> full-length critical analysis of Hopkins’s work

card.writes: It nudges the model toward words about interacting or engaging with something, such as interact, interaction and engagement.
card.plain: It fires in scholarly writing where the next word could be about engaging or interacting with texts and ideas.
